name: LMV7271MGX_NOPB
title: LMV7271, LMV7272, LMV7275: 1.8 V low-power comparators, single and dual, rail-to-rail input
summary: Low-power CMOS-output comparators with bipolar inputs whose common-mode range reaches 0.1 V past both rails, running from 1.8 V to 5.5 V on single or split supplies. Each channel draws about 9 µA at 1.8 V, with 880 ns propagation delay at 20 mV overdrive. LMV7271 (push-pull) and LMV7275 (open drain) are singles in SC70-5 and SOT-23-5; LMV7272 is a push-pull dual in an 8-bump DSBGA. LMV7271MGX/NOPB is the LMV7271 in SC70-5 (DCK) on a 3000-piece reel, marked C34.
key_figures: 9 µA typ, 12 µA max per channel at 1.8 V (LMV7271/LMV7275)
0.3 mV typ, 4 mV max; 6 mV max at the temperature extremes
−0.1 V to V+ + 0.1 V (1.9 V at 1.8 V supply)
tPHL 880 ns, tPLH 1100 ns at 20 mV overdrive; 570 ns / 800 ns at 50 mV
6 mA typ at 1.8 V, 34 mA typ at 5 V

notes: The LMV7271 and LMV7275 are single comparators, the LMV7272 a dual; the LMV7271 and LMV7272 have a push-pull output and the LMV7275 an open-drain output.
The marking of the LMV7272 sits on two lines, C over 01.
An automotive version, LMV7275-Q1, exists for the LMV7275.

circuits.title: Typical circuit
circuits.description: A single-supply comparator. VIN is divided by R1 and R2 onto the non-inverting input and compared with VREF on the inverting input; VOUT goes high while the divided input sits above VREF. C1 and C2 decouple the supply at the V+ pin.

circuits.title: Non-inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: The input reaches the non-inverting input through R1, and R2 feeds the output back to that same node VA, so the trip point moves with the output state. VREF sits on the inverting input. The output goes high when VIN climbs to VIN1 and low again when it falls to VIN2; the gap between them is VCC·R1/R2. RL is the load.

parts.note: feedback; set by the threshold equations

circuits.title: Inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: VIN drives the inverting input. R1 from the 5 V supply and R2 to ground set the threshold node VA on the non-inverting input, and R3 from the output to VA shifts it: with the output high R3 is in parallel with R1, giving VA1; with it low R3 is in parallel with R2, giving VA2. RLOAD is the load.
notes: R3 between 100 and 1000 times R1||R2 at 5 V, or 30 to 300 times at 1.8 V, gives a hysteresis of about 5 mV to 50 mV.

circuits.title: Simple zero-crossing detector
circuits.description: The inverting input is grounded and an AC signal of 100 mVPP drives the non-inverting input against ground; the output changes state each time the signal passes 0 V.
notes: U1 runs from V+ and ground.

circuits.title: Zero-crossing detector with hysteresis
circuits.description: R4 from VCC and R5 to ground set V1 on the non-inverting input, and the large R6 from the output to that node adds a little positive feedback (ΔV1 under 10 mV) for clean edges. The input comes to the inverting input V2 through R1 and R2, with R3 from VCC; with R1 + R2 equal to R5 the trip point V1 = V2 falls at VIN = 0. D1 at the R1-R2 junction clamps it near −700 mV, which with R2 and R3 keeps V2 from going below ground.

parts.note: positive feedback, much larger than R5

notes: Misprint: R4 should join V1, the divider with R5, not the inverting input V2.

circuits.title: Threshold detector
circuits.description: R1 and R2 divide VIN onto the non-inverting input; the inverting input is held at a steady VREF, and the output changes state as the divided input crosses VREF.
notes: U1 runs from V+ and ground.

circuits.title: Universal logic level shifter
circuits.description: Two 1 kΩ resistors split VA in half for the non-inverting input; the logic signal goes to the inverting input. The open-drain output is pulled up by REXT to VB, so the output swings to the second logic level, for instance a 3.3 V processor rail when VA is a 5 V analog rail.
notes: U1 runs from V+ and ground.

circuits.title: OR'ing the outputs
circuits.description: Four open-drain outputs share one 3.0 kΩ pull-up to V+. Whenever any one comparator pulls low, VO is low.
notes: U1 to U4 run from V+ and ground.

circuits.title: Square-wave oscillator
circuits.description: R1, R2 and R3 set the non-inverting input VA at 2VCC/3 while the output is high and VCC/3 while it is low. C1 charges and discharges through R4 from the output, and the comparator flips each time VC reaches VA, so VO is a square wave with f = 1/(2·R4·C1·ln2), about 10 kHz with these values. The 4.3 kΩ pull-up ties the output to V+.
notes: The free end of R1 returns to VCC in the threshold equations.
U1 runs from V+ and ground.
The highest usable frequency is set by the propagation delay and by the output slew rate under capacitive load.

circuits.title: Positive peak detector
circuits.description: The comparator runs as a unity-gain follower whose load is a hold capacitor: while VIN rises, the output charges C1 through the diode until the inverting input, tied to VOUT, catches up. The diode stops C1 discharging into the 1 kΩ pull-up, and R2 sets the decay. VOUT tops out at VCC − VF; a Schottky diode brings that headroom to about 300 mV. R1 is needed only with the open-drain LMV7275.

parts.note: pull-up; not needed on the LMV7271 or LMV7272

notes: C1 has its minus terminal at VOUT and its plus terminal at ground.
VOUT should be read through a high-impedance follower so it is not loaded.

circuits.title: Negative peak detector
circuits.description: The LMV7275's open-drain output sinks current into C1 and so holds the most negative input, between 0 V and −VCC; the inverting input follows VOUT. With no pull-up, C1 discharges only through the 1 MΩ R1 and any load, so R1 sets the decay. It needs a negative supply; +VCC may be grounded, since the output never rises above ground.

circuits.title: Window detector
circuits.description: R1, R2 and R3 in series from V+ to ground make VREF2 (upper) and VREF1 (lower). Comparator A has VREF2 on its non-inverting input and VIN on its inverting input; comparator B has VIN on its non-inverting input and VREF1 on its inverting input. Both outputs are high only while VREF1 < VIN < VREF2. Swapping each comparator's inputs flags a signal outside the window, and the open-drain LMV7275 lets the two outputs be tied into one.
notes: UA and UB run from V+ and ground.

operation.text: LMV7271 and LMV7275 are single comparators in SC70-5 and SOT-23-5; LMV7272 is a dual in an 8-bump DSBGA. The LMV7271 and LMV7272 have push-pull outputs; the LMV7275 output is open drain; its pull-up may go to as much as 5.5 V regardless of the LMV7275 supply, which serves level shifting and wired-OR. All three are characterised at 1.8 V, 2.7 V and 5 V, run from single or split supplies, and are made in a BiCMOS process with bipolar inputs and CMOS outputs.

Two input pairs, PNP and NPN, work in parallel, so the common-mode range runs from 0.1 V below V− to 0.1 V above V+. The NPN pair carries the input near V+ and the PNP pair near V−; the hand-over happens about 950 mV below V+. Each pair has its own offset, so VOS shifts with VCM, and keeping VCM clear of the crossover point is recommended.

No pull-up is needed, so supply current is only the quiescent current plus the load current. During each transition the PMOS and NMOS output devices conduct together for a moment, drawing a shoot-through current spike that can put glitches on the supply rails; supply bypass capacitors are required.

The LMV7275 is the LMV7271 without the upper P-channel output device. It needs a pull-up resistor to a positive voltage; with the output transistor off the pull-up sets the high level. Open-drain outputs can share one line as a wired-OR, and the pull-up may return to any voltage from V− to V+, which shifts the logic level.

Capacitive load does not change the propagation delay of the LMV7271 or LMV7272; resistive load changes the falling-edge delay a little, depending on its value. On the LMV7275 the rising-edge delay depends on the pull-up resistance and the load capacitance.
The gain is high: under 1 µV of input change swings the output fully, rail to rail. A noisy or slow input therefore needs hysteresis from positive feedback, or the output follows the noise.

Decouple the supply with 0.01 µF ceramic in parallel with 10 µF. The fast output edges draw peak currents that depend on load capacitance, and a poorly bypassed supply can ring through trace inductance and high-ESR capacitors. Treat the part as a high-speed device: short ground paths and small low-ESR ceramics right across V+ and V−. Average supply current rises above the quiescent value with output load capacitance and toggle rate.

Place a 0.1 µF ceramic right at the supply pins and 6.8 µF or more of tantalum where the supply enters the board; with split supplies put 0.1 µF between V+ and V−. Keep leads short and avoid loops, since output coupling into the inputs through stray capacitance causes oscillation during transitions. Use an unbroken ground plane, preferably under the part, with low-impedance paths for the heavier currents. Route the output away from the inputs with a topside ground guard between them. When one input is fed through a resistor network, give the other input a resistor of the same value and lay the input traces out symmetrically. Tie every pin of an unused comparator to the negative supply.

Direct sunlight, halogen lamps and backlights shining through the PCB can upset a DSBGA part; red and infrared light are the worst. A copper pour beneath the DSBGA, on an inner or bottom layer, shades it; vias under the part can let light through. Mounting follows application note AN-1112 (SNVA009).
LMV7272TLCONV is a two-layer DSBGA-to-DIP adapter for characterisation: the LMV7272 sits on the bottom side, and C1, a capacitor across the two supply rails, sits on the top side.

R6 is very large against R5 (2000 R5), so the hysteresis is small, ΔV1 under 10 mV, yet enough for fast output edges. D1 keeps the inverting input from going below about −100 mV; how far the input may be overdriven below ground depends on how much current D1 can handle.
Built-in ESD protection is limited: store and handle the parts with leads shorted or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
